questions.prompt: Why are the coefficients of (x + y)ⁿ symmetric (the same read forward and backward)?
questions.prompt_markup: Why are the coefficients of (x + y)ⁿ symmetric (the same read forward and backward)?

choices.text: C(n, k) = C(n, n - k): choosing which k of the n factors give x is the same as choosing which n - k give y.
x and y always have equal values in the expansion, so the coefficients of matching terms are the same.
The middle coefficient is always the largest one, so the list of coefficients must be symmetric.

questions.correct_answer: C(n, k) = C(n, n - k): choosing which k of the n factors give x is the same as choosing which n - k give y.
questions.grading_note: The count C(n, k) is symmetric. The others are false ((x + y)² = x² + 2xy + y²) or do not explain the symmetry.
